newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: FIRST "BOERS" ARRIVE IN MOZAMBIQUE ON LATEST TREK.
newsitem.headline: FIRST "BOERS" ARRIVE IN MOZAMBIQUE ON LATEST TREK.

text.p: The first 13 South Africans who intend to set up farms in Mozambique have arrived in the northern province of Niassa, Radio Mozambique reported on Saturday.

It said the farmers would occupy land that once belonged to the Matama state farm just outside the provincial capital, Lichinga, and would set up "experimental farms" to produce seeds for the 1997-98 agricultural year.
Later, more South Africans are expected to settle on 100,000 hectares of land in Niassa's Lugenda river valley.
The settlement programme has been dubbed by the press as "the new trek", since most if not all of the settlers will be whites of Afrikaner origin.
President Nelson Mandela of South Africa and President Joaquim Chissano of Mozambique signed an agreement on the plan in Maputo last May.
The aim is to take South African know-how and investment to Niassa, a fertile province the size of England with a population of less than 800,000.
